source: Morais O., Cargill C., Parke K. and Barnes T. 2020. Smallholder Pig Production Technicians' Manual. Timor-Leste Ministry of Agriculture and Fisheries, University of Queensland, ACIAR and the TOMAK Program (Australian Aid), Dili.
text: A good pen gives pigs a choice of two environments: a clean, dry area for sleeping (covered with soft bedding like dry grass, especially important for pigs under 12 weeks) and a separate wet area for eating, drinking, urinating, and defecating. Place the water trough in the wet area to encourage pigs to relieve themselves there, with the floor sloping slightly so water drains away. Food troughs should have a solid base fixed to the floor so pigs can't tip them over. The best floors are solid concrete (roughened so it isn't slippery when wet) sloping at a minimum of 1-in-20 from the dry sleeping area toward the wet area and a drain.
caveat: This guidance comes from a Timor-Leste smallholder pig manual, not a Cambodia-specific source. Feed ingredients and general husbandry practices transfer well to Cambodia's tropical smallholder conditions, but local breed weights/ages and disease-context details may differ; confirm specifics with a local vet or extension officer where precision matters.
